clue.text: Let Ulster lag provoke argument

definitions.meaning: an Ulster is a long heavy outer garment; letting one drag along the ground behind you is the old Irish gesture of daring others to tread on it
to pick a quarrel deliberately, by inviting someone to take offence

explanation.surface: An instruction to allow Northern Ireland to fall behind is said to stir up dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulster' reads as the province but is the long overcoat named after it; the idiom comes from the brawler who dragged his coat for someone to step on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to court a fight on purpose, from the challenge of daring anyone to step on a garment dragged behind.

clue.text: Intimidation i.e. imprisoning leaders of rival enterprises

indicators.note: imprisoning says the abbreviation's expansion holds the picked letters inside it

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: leaders of picks out the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Bullying by imprisoning the bosses of competing firms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders of' gives R and E, and 'imprisoning' puts them inside THAT'S, the meaning of i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Menacing statements are a means of bullying or coercion.

clue.text: Saw outside vehicle beginning to take lead

indicators.note: outside says the proverb word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or adage
a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word take

explanation.surface: A carpenter's saw on the outside of a van starts to edge ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the noun for a proverb, not a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an advantage in a contest means being in the lead, a synonym.

clue.text: Money a sucker progressively reduces

definitions.meaning: a lollipop on a stick shrinks as a child licks and sucks it

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for cash and also short for a lollipop that gets smaller as it is sucked.

clue.text: Bushranger related to elusive Manxman?

definitions.meaning: an Australian outback outlaw; the most famous wore home-made iron armour
the old music-hall song asks whether anybody has seen a missing man from the Isle of Man; the outlaw shares his surname

explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song 'Has Anybody Here Seen Kelly?' is about a Manxman 'Kelly from the Isle of Man'; the question mark marks the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the famous nineteenth-century Australian outlaw hanged in Melbourne in 1880.

clue.text: Son needs babywear that's neat and elegant

parts.note: a nappy is the British word for a diaper

explanation.surface: A son wears a nappy that is smart.
explanation.walkthrough: NAPPY is the British word for a baby's diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy is used of dress meaning smart and stylish.

clue.text: Old clue — do get solution right

parts.note: a key is a clue that unlocks a mystery
a key gives the solution, as with an answer key

explanation.surface: Solvers are told to work out an ancient clue correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: KEY appears twice, once from 'clue' and once from 'solution'; 'do' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal way of saying all right, signalling agreement.

clue.text: Put down figures in columns

definitions.meaning: to put forward a motion or bill for discussion in a parliament
numbers arranged in rows and columns

explanation.definitionFit: To table a motion is to propose it, and a table is a grid of numbers.

clue.text: Crush is a drink

definitions.meaning: to stamp out or put an end to, as with a rumour
whisky from north of the border

explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour is to crush it, and Scotch is whisky.

clue.text: Ran down and back to assist at birth

indicators.note: back tells us the word for helping at a birth is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a midwife delivers a baby

explanation.surface: Someone ran down a hill and then hurried back to help at a birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DELIVER round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to criticise or abuse them, a synonym.

clue.text: Be calm? I can become still

indicators.note: can become says the letters of the preceding words turn into something new when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soothing instruction to stay calm so that one may become quiet and motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like an adjective meaning motionless, but it is the noun: a distilling apparatus. 'can become' rearranges BECALM plus I.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling vessel, so it is a kind of still used by alchemists.

clue.text: Small number in some trouble

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you any?'
NO is the short form of number

explanation.surface: A handful of people find themselves in a spot of bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' is the verb (to bother), not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to irritate or bother them, a synonym.

clue.text: Suitable as husband no longer, Gable's not married

parts.note: a former husband is an ex

indicators.note: not married removes the letter M, the abbreviation for married, from the gable word

parts.note: a pediment is the triangular gable over a classical portico

explanation.surface: A woman finds Clark Gable no longer fit to be her husband since he is not married.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gable' suggests the film star Clark Gable but is the architectural gable; M is the standard abbreviation for married.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expedient is advantageous or appropriate for the purpose, close to fitting.

clue.text: Raised platform round eating-house is disposed of

indicators.note: round says the word for disposed of goes around the cafe word

parts.note: goods disposed of are sold
a caff is British slang for a cheap cafe

explanation.surface: A raised stage around a restaurant has been got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised platform' suggests a stage, but think of the gallows; the cheap British cafe goes into a word for disposed of.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffold is an elevated wooden stage, such as that used for executions.

clue.text: Fallen arch, for instance — it can rule out service

definitions.meaning: a fallen arch is a defect of the lower limb
in tennis, stepping over the baseline while serving makes that serve invalid

explanation.walkthrough: 'service' sounds like work or military duty, but is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally it is a defect of the lower limb; in tennis it is an infringement that cancels the serve.

clue.text: Draft first of seamen to sailing vessel

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word seamen

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: The first sailors are sent to man a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draft' suggests sending sailors (drafting crew), but it is the definition, a rough outline.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough preliminary drawing or outline, a synonym of draft.

clue.text: Destroying angel, perhaps, has lots to do — a devastation

indicators.note: devastation says the letters of the preceding words are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruinous angel has plenty to do to wreak havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: The destroying angel is a deadly white fungus, not a biblical figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The destroying angel is a deadly Amanita mushroom, an example of a poisonous fungus.

clue.text: Handle the wrong way African seaman bound by agreement

indicators.note: the wrong way says the whole assembled piece is read backwards
bound by says the seaman is held within the agreement word

parts.note: a bond is a binding agreement
the Kroo (Kru) are a West African people famed as seamen

explanation.surface: A sailor from Africa held to a contract handles things badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns BONKROOD round. The Kroo of Liberia and the West African coast served widely as sailors on European ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorknob is the round handle used to open a door.

clue.text: French chap in British school

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is enrolled in a British school.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON is the English public school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A Breton is a man from Brittany in north-west France.

clue.text: Suited hard worker, entering academic stream

indicators.note: entering links the worker and the stream so that one sits within the other

parts.note: a bee is a byword for industry, as in busy bee
the Cam is the river flowing through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A diligent student, dressed up, joins a university stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's 'entering' is loose: it is the Cambridge river that goes inside the worker. 'Suited' is not about clothes but about fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: If a hat became you, it suited or flattered you, a synonym.

clue.text: Put glass behind to see this hairstyle

parts.note: a pony is a small measure or glass of drink
tail means the rear or behind

explanation.surface: Place a drinking glass behind you to see a hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is a small glass of beer or liqueur in British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered bunch of hair tied at the back of the head is a familiar hairdo.

clue.text: Permit silence to be broken

indicators.note: to be broken says the letters of silence are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A request to allow a quiet to be interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Permit' is a verb here, matching the American-spelt verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To license something is to authorise or allow it formally.

clue.text: Old magistrate has to seek advice endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the word for seeking advice is dropped

parts.note: to consult is to seek advice

explanation.surface: An ancient judge needs to ask for guidance repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' suggests forever but means drop the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul was one of the two chief magistrates of the Roman Republic.

clue.text: Cereal ground in plant, say

indicators.note: say tells us the plant name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a blue-flowered plant of cornfields

explanation.surface: Grain is being milled inside a factory, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is a flowering plant whose name sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the finely milled starch of maize, a ground cereal used for thickening.

clue.text: Two rivers merging in the country

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: Two rivers meet somewhere in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The two rivers are R and the Ural.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things of the countryside, away from towns.

clue.text: Simple part of job, as I concede

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Admitting that some of the work is straightforward.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary or plain, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Incidentally, abandoning the side road here

indicators.note: abandoning says the word the is dropped from the phrase meaning incidentally

parts.note: a three-word phrase used to introduce an aside, meaning incidentally
taken as written

explanation.surface: By the way, someone has left the minor road at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove THE from BY THE WAY, the phrase for incidentally.
explanation.definitionFit: A byway is a minor road or lane off the main route.

clue.text: Resistance surrounding king's title

indicators.note: surrounding says the Resistance word goes around the letter for king

parts.note: the Maquis was the French Resistance in the Second World War
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: The Resistance encircles a monarch's name of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' reads as electrical, but is the wartime French underground, the Maquis.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquis is a nobleman ranking between duke and earl, so the word is a noble rank.

clue.text: Very young bishop overwhelmed by spreading renown

indicators.note: overwhelmed by says the bishop letter is swallowed up by the other piece
spreading indicates the letters of renown are spread around into a new order

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A youthful bishop is overwhelmed by his growing fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges RENOWN into NEWORN, and 'overwhelmed by' puts B inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn has only just come into the world, so is as young as can be.

clue.text: Small version of Gainsborough picture, it's said, in nursery

definitions.text: Small version of Gainsborough picture, it's said, in nursery

parts.words: Small version of Gainsborough picture, it's said, in nursery
parts.note: Gainsborough's famous portrait shows a lad in azure satin; swap its two title words and prefix a word for small to get the name of a figure from a children's rhyme

explanation.surface: A miniature copy of a famous Gainsborough painting hangs in a child's room.
explanation.walkthrough: Gainsborough's portrait is The Blue Boy; 'nursery' points to the nursery rhyme whose character's name reworks that title.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure is the sleepy shepherd lad of a traditional English nursery rhyme.
